title: Continuous Subarray Sum
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums contains a subarray of at least two consecutive elements whose sum is a multiple of k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if nums contains a subarray of at least two consecutive elements whose sum is a multiple of k. A subarray is defined as a contiguous part of the array, and an integer x is considered a multiple of k if there exists an integer n such that x = n * k. Note that 0 is always a multiple of k.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 2^31-1. The selected subarray must be contiguous and contain at least TWO elements.
Its sum may be any multiple of k, including zero; it need not equal k.
hints: Equal prefix remainders identify sums divisible by k.
Keep the earliest index for each remainder, and require the two prefix positions to be at least two apart.
Initialize first[0]=-1. Accumulate modulo k; if a seen remainder is far enough away return true; otherwise insert only an unseen remainder.
Do not overwrite the earliest position. Zero is a valid multiple, but a single zero still fails the length requirement.
editorial: The difference between two prefixes is divisible by k exactly when their remainders agree. For each current prefix the earliest equal remainder gives the longest possible segment, so discarding later occurrences cannot lose a solution. Initial remainder zero at index -1 handles a segment starting at index zero. The independent oracle enumerates every contiguous subarray of length at least two and tests its literal sum.

tests.explanation: The adjacent values [2,4] sum to 6, a multiple of k, and have the required length two.
Return false. The lone 6 is divisible by 6 but is too short; the only two-element subarray sums to 7.
